title: What Does Bona Certified Craftsman Mean, and Why Does It Matter for Your Floors?
meta: A Bona Certified Craftsman is a refinisher trained on the full Bona system, dust containment to finish. Wills Flooring explains what it means in Kirkland.
keywords: Bona Certified Craftsman meaning, what is Bona certified flooring contractor, Bona Traffic HD vs Mega, Bona finish hardwood floors, hardwood floor refinishing Kirkland WA, how to choose a floor refinisher

blocks.lead: A Bona Certified Craftsman is a flooring contractor trained and vetted by Bona, the Swedish finish and equipment maker, to refinish floors using the complete Bona system: dust containment, abrasives, sealers and finishes, applied the way Bona specifies.
blocks.detail: It matters because most refinishing failures are process failures, not product failures. Wills Flooring holds the certification and refinishes at $3.99 per sq ft natural, $6.50 with stain and $1.99 for a screen and recoat, all with Bona water-based finishes.

blocks.html: Kirkland homeowners comparing refinishing quotes see "Bona Certified Craftsman" on some websites and not others, and reasonably ask whether it is a real credential or a logo anyone can paste on a truck. It is real, it is earned, and it tells you specific things about how your floor will be done. It also does not tell you everything. This post explains what the program is, what changes on your floor when a certified crew does the work, and the questions the badge does not answer that you should still ask.

items.title: Who Bona is
items.text: Bona has made hardwood floor finishes and sanding equipment since 1919 and is the name behind Traffic HD, the commercial-grade water-based finish most premium refinishers use. It sells to contractors, not just at retail, and has a direct interest in floors finished with its products holding up.

items.title: What a certified contractor commits to
items.text: Certification means the crew has been trained on Bona's system and uses it from start to finish: Bona dust containment, Bona abrasives, Bona sealers and finishes, applied at Bona's spread rates and dry times. Mixing brands or skipping the sealer is how you lose the badge.

items.title: Why the system matters more than any product
items.text: A finish is only as good as the sealer under it and the sanding scratch pattern under that. Bona tests its sealers and finishes together, so a certified crew is not guessing about compatibility, adhesion or how a stain will react with the top coat.

items.title: Technical backing
items.text: Certified contractors have a direct line to Bona's technical team. If a floor does something strange, and old Kirkland floors sometimes do, there is a manufacturer chemist on the phone rather than a guess.

blocks.text: What changes on your floor when a certified crew does the work

Typical uncertified approach

Whatever is on sale, sometimes oil-based over a water-based sealer

blocks.note: None of this is exotic. It is discipline. The certification is Bona confirming that a contractor follows it every time, not just on the floors that get photographed.

blocks.text: The Bona finishes you will hear about, in plain English

items.html: Bona Traffic HD. The commercial-grade two-component finish. Highest wear and chemical resistance in the line, dries clear, very low odor. This is what we recommend for Kirkland family homes with dogs and for anyone who wants the floor to look the same in year eight.
Bona Mega and Mega One. Single-component finishes that cure with oxygen from the air. Excellent durability for residential use, easier to recoat later, and a step down in price from Traffic HD.
Bona Naturale. The lowest sheen option, designed to make the floor look like bare sanded wood. Popular in Houghton and Juanita remodels chasing a Scandinavian look on white oak.

Bona DriFast stain and Bona Red Out. DriFast is the stain line that lets us finish-coat the same day. Red Out is a treatment that neutralizes the pink in red oak so it can take a pale, modern color without going salmon.
Bona sealers. NaturalSeal, ClassicSeal and IntenseSeal set the base tone under the clear finish. Choosing the sealer is the most underrated design decision in a natural refinish.

blocks.text: What the badge does not tell you

items.title: It is not a license or insurance
items.text: Bona certifies process, not legal standing. Check the contractor's Washington L&I registration and ask for proof of liability insurance separately. Wills Flooring has been licensed and insured since 2013 and will send the documents before you sign.

items.title: It does not judge the estimate
items.text: A certified crew can still measure badly or quote the whole house when only 700 sq ft is being sanded. Insist on measured square footage and a written scope. A firm price on the spot is the standard we hold ourselves to.

items.title: It does not fix a floor that should not be sanded
items.text: Thin fir in an older Kirkland home or an engineered floor with a 1 mm veneer cannot be saved by good technique. A trustworthy contractor tells you that at the estimate, badge or no badge.

items.title: It is not a substitute for reviews
items.text: Read the Google reviews and look for photos of finished floors under daylight, not showroom light. Our 4.8-star rating across 100+ five-star reviews is public; any contractor's record should be.

blocks.title: The Kirkland resale angle:
blocks.text: Eastside buyers and their inspectors notice finish quality. Swirl marks near baseboards, a cloudy topcoat or a floor that smells of solvent for a week are the things that turn up in inspection reports and price negotiations. A water-based Bona system finish in Rose Hill or Bridle Trails is a small line item against a sale price, and the finish is one of the first things a buyer touches.
How to verify a certification and what to ask next

items.html: Ask which Bona sealer and finish they plan to use, and why. A certified crew will name the products and explain the look. "Polyurethane" is not an answer.

Ask how dust is contained. Vacuum-connected sanders should be standard. Wills adds full plastic sealing and an air scrubber as a $250 option for occupied homes and condos, including the elevator-access buildings in downtown Kirkland.

Ask for dry times in writing. Sock traffic at 24 hours, furniture at 72 is our normal schedule for a natural finish. Anyone promising furniture back the next morning is either using a different product or skipping coats.
Get the coat count on the quote. Sealer plus three coats of finish is our standard. Two coats total is a common way to hit a lower number.
Compare warranties, not just prices. Our guide to comparing refinishing quotes in Kirkland walks through the line items. Full service details are on the refinishing page.

faq.q: Is Bona Certified Craftsman a real certification?
faq.a: Yes. It is a contractor program run by Bona, the finish and equipment manufacturer. Contractors are trained on the Bona system and commit to using Bona dust containment, abrasives, sealers and finishes together. It is not a government license, so verify L&I registration and insurance separately.

faq.q: Does a Bona certified refinish cost more?
faq.a: Not at Wills Flooring. Our published rates, $3.99 per sq ft natural, $6.50 with stain and $1.99 for a screen and recoat, already include Bona sealer and three coats of Bona water-based finish. The certification is how we work, not an upgrade line.

faq.q: What is the difference between Bona Traffic HD and Bona Mega?
faq.a: Traffic HD is a two-component commercial finish with the highest scratch and chemical resistance and the lowest odor. Mega is a single-component residential finish that is very durable and simpler to recoat later. Homes with large dogs or heavy traffic benefit most from Traffic HD.

faq.q: Are Bona finishes safe for kids and pets?
faq.a: Bona water-based finishes are low-VOC and GREENGUARD certified, with far less odor than oil-based polyurethane. We recommend keeping pets off the floor until the 24-hour sock-traffic point and waiting for the full cure before putting rugs down.

faq.q: Can a Bona system finish go over an older oil-based floor?
faq.a: For a screen and recoat, yes, provided the old finish is intact and properly abraded, and we test adhesion first. Wax or acrylic residue can cause peeling, which is one of the things we check at the estimate before quoting the $1.99 recoat rate.

faq.q: How do I confirm a contractor is actually Bona certified?
faq.a: Ask them directly which Bona products they use and how they contain dust; certified crews answer specifically. You can also ask for their certification and check the contractor listings Bona publishes. Wills Flooring is happy to show ours at the estimate.
